search-batch.description: Multiple queries in input order against one saved search index snapshot. Shared index metadata and failures occur once at the outer level. The outer revision pins the ordered query list and index snapshot. Per-query revisions support individual searches. Normal presentation may omit trailing hits while retaining every query; omitted fields are explicit.

tables.description: Tables listed once for all queries, as search-passage table with the document of their rows: document_id, source_path, state and structure_reviewed (and extraction_path with --full). A row names its table by table_ref; rows of one table under other headings name other entries. A table that did not fit lists omitted_fields.

search-profile.description: Disjoint wall-clock milliseconds emitted to stderr by documents search --profile after stdout. Batch timings cover all queries against one saved index snapshot. total_ms starts immediately before Store::search_many, excluding CLI startup, argument parsing and project opening; response_ms includes payload decoding, CLI formatting and stdout emission. other_ms covers unassigned internal overhead. Timings exclude emitting this diagnostic record.

setup_ms.description: Query analysis and read-only database opening.

integrity_ms.description: Saved index metadata reads and revision calculation; canonical files are not checked by search.

index_update_ms.description: Read-only transaction completion; search does not update the index.

sql_ms.description: Result count, SQL preparation, ranking, deduplication ordering and stepping the result cursor; for a page after the first, reading or saving its ranking and reading its passages.

search-format.description: One value of a format property of the indexed text, an item of documents search-formats. Values are as the adopted extraction resolves them: one per cell or shape text, mixed where its runs differ. Properties come in the order color, theme, font, size, bold, italic, underline, strike, highlight, fill, each with the most hits first. A mark holds where every run of the text shows it; fill is a filled cell behind the text.

value.description: Font color as RRGGBB, auto or mixed; theme slot of the color; latin or East Asian font name or mixed; size in points or mixed; true for a mark (bold, italic, underline, strike, highlight, fill).

family.description: For a color, the family a --color filter names it by; auto is black.

hits.description: The hits of a search filtering by this value alone.

cells.description: The cells and shape texts with text in this value.

search-synonyms.description: Explicit bidirectional project vocabulary groups; expansion applies to whole whitespace-delimited query terms only, without recursion.

search-state.description: State stored in the search index. CLI search responses omit verification hashes, including with --full.

search-passage.description: Fragment stored in the search index. CLI search responses omit extraction_sha256, including with --full. Source pointers are relative to extraction.json; offsets are Unicode scalar offsets in the displayed extracted text, not original file bytes.

table.description: The interpreted table a row belongs to. Headings and within come from the tables it is nested in, outermost first.

headings.description: Column headers of enclosing tables above this table, each after the headers above it.

within.description: Cells of the enclosing tables' records this table belongs to, by row and column.

columns.description: One entry per value, in column order: the cell's column and the column headers above it. Headers in the row itself are values, not headers.

values.description: Every cell of the row in table.columns order, as the original shows it, an empty cell as an empty string. unread names why a cell is unread or uncalculated; an unread cell keeps its extracted text, and is null without one, as an uncalculated formula is. A row too long for one passage lists the pieces of this passage, without its empty cells.

row_context.description: Row headers of other rows that head this row, such as a merged item name or a section row, outermost first.

unread.description: Cells of the row by address without a known text: a reader could not read it or has not examined it, or a formula was saved without its result.

formatted.description: On a hit of a search with a format filter: the sources of this passage whose text is in the format, in source order; a cell by its address, a shape's text by its pointer.

headers.description: Header texts, those higher in the header chain first, then by row and column.

text.description: The text the original shows. A workbook cell shows its value, for a formula its result, under its number format.

value.description: The stored value of a workbook cell, when it reads otherwise than text.

formula.description: The formula of a workbook cell. Its result is the stored value; a formula saved without one shows no text.

format.description: The index's ID of the format of the source's text; stored only, responses leave it out.
